title: N70 Nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud
caption: The N 70 superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This three-colour image shows N 70, a glowing superbubble of interstellar gas in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way in the southern sky. The bubble is about 300 light-years across.

N 70 was blown out by winds from hot, massive stars and by supernova explosions, and its interior is filled with thin, hot gas that is still expanding. Objects like this give astronomers an excellent chance to study how the life cycles of stars are linked to the way whole galaxies evolve.

Very massive stars have a big effect on their surroundings. Their winds and explosions stir and mix the clouds of gas and dust between the stars. In doing so they leave a lasting mark on where future generations of stars and planetary systems will form, and on what those new stars will be made of.

understand.summary: This image comes from the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope, using B, V and hydrogen-alpha filters in visible light. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.
filters: 429 nm · Optical B (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
554 nm · Optical V (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
656 nm · Optical H-alpha (Very Large Telescope FORS2)
understand.eye: The hydrogen filter isolates the glow of the gas, and the telescope's exposures reveal a bubble far too faint to see by eye.

explore: The image was built from CCD frames taken with the FORS2 instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope. ESO's caption puts the Large Magellanic Cloud at about 160,000 light-years from us.
alt: A glowing bubble of gas among stars.
